cap: Membrane receptors turn an outside signal into an inside messenger. Gs raises cAMP to activate protein kinase A and Gi lowers it; Gq splits a membrane lipid into IP3, which releases calcium, and DAG, which activates protein kinase C; tyrosine kinase receptors phosphorylate proteins themselves or through JAK. Steroids, thyroid hormone and calcitriol cross the membrane and change gene transcription, so their effects start slowly and last.
teach: Read each column from the top down: the hormone binds, a G protein or kinase switches on, and a messenger spreads the signal. The receptor, not the hormone, picks the column, which is why ADH appears twice: V2 receptors in the collecting duct use Gs and cAMP, while V1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle use Gq, IP3 and calcium.
